entries.name: Seated Dumbbell Palms-Down Wrist Curl
entries.reason: Source-bound side-view draft with a hand that bends at the wrist. Sitting on the edge of a flat bench, leaning forward with the forearms level along the thighs and the wrists just past the knees; only the hands move, from dropped to lifted and slowly back, with the dumbbells held under the knuckles because the palms face down. Not drawn: a close-up of the hand. The catalogue asks for one, and this frame shows the whole seated figure, so the wrist movement is small on screen.
entries.summary: Forearms flat on the thighs, palms down: let the wrists drop, lift the backs of the hands as far as they go without moving the elbows, then lower slowly.

frames.caption: Sit on the edge of a flat bench with the forearms resting on the thighs, palms facing down, wrists just past the knees. Let the wrists drop.
Lift the backs of the hands as far as the range allows without the elbows moving.
Keep the forearms flat and still.
When the elbows lift to help, reduce the load.

entries.name: Seated Dumbbell Palms-Up Wrist Curl
entries.reason: Source-bound side-view draft with a hand that bends at the wrist. Sitting on the edge of a flat bench, leaning forward with the forearms level along the thighs and the wrists just past the knees; only the hands move, from open under the load to curled up and slowly back, with the dumbbells resting on top of the hands because the palms face up. Not drawn: a close-up of the hand. The catalogue asks for one, and this frame shows the whole seated figure, so the wrist movement is small on screen.
entries.summary: Forearms flat on the thighs, palms up: let the wrists open, curl the palms up as far as they go without moving the elbows, then lower slowly into the stretch.

frames.caption: Sit on the edge of a flat bench with the forearms resting on the thighs, palms facing up, wrists just past the knees. Let the wrists open under the load.
Curl the palms up as far as the range allows without the elbows moving.
Keep the forearms flat and still.
When the elbows lift to help, reduce the load.
